title: Manufacturing, transporting or transferring an assault weapon
summary: Knowingly manufacturing or causing to be manufactured, distributing, transporting, importing into California, keeping for sale, offering or exposing for sale, giving or lending an assault weapon within the conduct covered by Penal Code section 30600(a), without an applicable statutory authorization or exemption. The prosecution must prove knowledge of the conduct and that the person knew or reasonably should have known the weapon had the characteristics bringing it within the statutory definition. The weapon must meet the applicable statutory assault-weapon definition; a generic firearm description is insufficient. Mere possession is addressed by separate provisions. Registration alone is not blanket permission to sell, lend or transport the weapon: the exact conduct must satisfy the applicable registration, permit or exemption conditions. Those conditions can include authorized official use, permitted manufacture or sales, specified estate dispositions, supervised lending, qualifying nonresident competitions, and authorized importation or transport. The conduct date, weapon characteristics, permit or registration documents and any applicable court orders must be checked.
penalty: Felony: 4, 6 or 8 years under Penal Code section 1170(h), subject to its state-prison exclusions. If no other offense-specific fine is prescribed, section 672 permits an additional discretionary base fine up to $10,000. Under section 30600(b), transferring, lending, selling or giving the weapon to a minor in violation of subdivision (a) adds one consecutive year under section 1170(h). Section 30600(c) provides a distinct offense for each weapon; its narrow first-violation exception refers to sections 30605 and 30610 and is not a general exception for section 30600(a). Section 30615 may add a consecutive year when another crime is committed while violating the article. These are separate punishment provisions, not a guarantee that every enhancement applies or a single maximum for the entire case. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and other case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Knowledge of the prohibited conduct and knowledge, or reasonable grounds to know, the characteristics making the weapon an assault weapon or .50 BMG rifle; applicable authorization and exemptions remain material.
